# ots.golf

> A competition on the worst-case verification cost, in compressions, of hash-based one-time
> signatures with a 128-bit public key, signatures of at most 5504 bits and 127-bit security.
> Three lower classes and two upper tracks are open: compressions for any algorithm, and
> cycles for a verified RISC-V implementation. Certificates are checked by the Lean kernel.

Public tracks, from broadest to most restricted lower class:

| Track | Slug | Schemes | Checked claim |
|---|---|---|---:|
| Generality 3/3 | generic-lower | Any admissible oracle algorithm | 1 |
| Generality 2/3 | lower | Fixed DAGs with arbitrary deterministic functions and disclosure cuts | 18 |
| Generality 1/3 | disclosure-lower | Whole-word DAGs: 128-bit secrets, 256-bit hashes, fixed halves and concatenation | 93 |
| Upper bound | generic-upper | Any admissible oracle algorithm | 106 |
| RISC-V upper bound | riscv-upper | An admissible OTS with an RV64IM verifier proved equivalent to its specification; cycles on accepting executions | 9041 |

Lower claims are universal within their class; larger is better. Upper claims construct a scheme;
smaller is better. Each lower class has its own record. The Upper bound
certificate proves perfect correctness, signing failure at most 2^-128, 127-bit strong security,
all resource limits and a worst-case verification cost of 106 compressions. Generality 3/3 lower
uses the same signing-failure limit of 2^-128 and strong unforgeability. Both availability requirements
are averaged over honest key generation and signing for every public-key-dependent message choice.
The RISC-V certificate additionally proves that the fixed machine image's complete oracle computation
equals the Lean verifier on every public key, message and raw signature, that every execution
terminates, and that accepting executions take at most 9041 cycles. Ordinary instructions,
RANDOM and HALT cost one cycle; HASH costs max(1, ceil(bits/512)) on the shared oracle. Rejecting
executions are unscored.

All parties share one random oracle on bit strings, returning 256 bits. Equal inputs always share
an answer across all uses. Input lengths include explicit parameters and tweaks. Each query
costs one compression per started 512-bit input block, at least one.
Messages are 256 bits; key generation costs at most 1024 compressions and signing at most 2^20.
Deterministic computation and randomness are free. The protected Lean interfaces define the exact
security experiments; AGENTS.md lists submission requirements.

Submission roots are formal/Submissions/GenericLower, Lower, DisclosureLower, GenericUpper and
RiscvUpper, respectively. The Upper and DisclosureUpper roots remain historical reference certificates at
106, with closed public admission.

Submit a pull request to leanEthereum/ots.golf-submissions changing only one admitted submission root. It must be flat, include
Solution.lean and claim.txt, obey import and size limits, and use the pinned toolchain. Exported
proofs may use only propext, Quot.sound and Classical.choice: no sorry or native_decide.
Optional PR-body lines `Assisted by: <model>` and `Co-authors: a, b` provide attribution.
A verified improvement becomes a record only when that exact head is merged.

The model, verifier, website and reference certificates live in leanEthereum/ots.golf-dev.
The submissions repository contains the five public roots and a pinned .contract submodule of
the core. Clone it with --recurse-submodules. Local checks from that repository, replacing
generic-upper with another track slug as needed:

    .contract/verifier/setup_tools.sh
    (cd .contract/formal && lake exe cache get && lake build OptimalOTS)
    python3 .contract/verifier/verify.py generic-upper --source .

The hosted verifier takes only the chosen root from the PR head. Its trusted model and verifier
come from the core checkout; submission merges update records in the submissions repository.

macOS proof checks run unsandboxed for trusted local development. Production requires the Linux isolation
and launch checks in service/deploy/README.md. Lower filters affect only lower leaderboards;
the compression chart has three lower series and one Upper bound series; the RISC-V chart has its
own cycle axis. Rules contain no current scores.
Local Satoshi/Vitalik/Hal Finney rows are clearly fictional demos, never verified submissions; preserve them
and refresh localhost after commits. Never push or deploy without authorization.

- Core: https://github.com/leanEthereum/ots.golf-dev (site: https://ots.golf)
- Proof PRs: https://github.com/leanEthereum/ots.golf-submissions
- Exact submission requirements and exports: AGENTS.md
- Track metadata, limits and protected files: challenges.json
- Interfaces: formal/OptimalOTS/{Algorithm,AlgorithmWeak,Statement,WholeWords,RiscvMachine,Riscv}.lean
- Proof guides: docs/{generic-lower,lower-bound-proof,whole-words,generic-upper,riscv-upper}.md
- Official verifier: verifier/verify.py
